messages:
Alex (CEO): Thanks everyone for joining the all‑hands today — leaving this thread open for any follow-ups on mission/positioning/competitors. I'll answer what I can, and leadership will chime in. :wave:
Priya (CTO): Quick technical framing question — how prescriptive do we want to be about runtime choices in our docs? e.g. recommend kernel builds + quant profiles vs. leaving it neutral.
Sam (Product): From product POV we should give strong defaults for common workloads (chat, embeddings) and an "advanced tuning" section. Customers like prescriptive recipes.
Jordan (Eng): Agree with Sam. We can publish 2-3 reference configs per HW class. Low friction + measurable perf wins.
Taylor (PM): A follow-up: for go-to-market messaging, are we leaning into "cost predictability" or "performance parity across environments" as the headline?
Alex (CEO): Headline should be "predictable inference economics" — cost + latency + reliability. But messaging should pivot by audience: infra/platform teams care about parity and controls; product teams care about latency & dev velocity.
Ravi (Sales): Helpful. For enterprise deals, customers ask directly about fallbacks and private deployment SLAs — can we put a simple one-pager for SAs?
Marta (People Ops): Slightly off-topic but a few folks asked about recording and FAQ for new hires who missed the all‑hands. Can we store these follow-ups in a shared doc?
deploy-bot: transcript uploaded: https://redwood.internal/transcripts/allhands-1805554321 (auto-note)
Priya (CTO): On competitors: big cloud managed endpoints = simpler for model access, but our edge is optimized serving + unified ops across hosted/dedicated/private. We should call out specific ROI examples (tokens/$ and p95 latency).
Sam (Product): Can we get 2 anonymized customer mini-case studies (startup and mid-market) showing before/after cost and latency improvements? Those are convincing in sales decks.
Jordan (Eng): Technical ask: can infra publish a short benchmark matrix with sequence lengths, batching, model versions, and kernel types for top 5 models? That will make our claims concrete.
Alex (CEO): Yes — Priya/Eng and Product will collaborate. Sam: own the case studies. Jordan: produce the benchmark table. We'll aim to publish a one‑pager and the FAQ by end of next week.
Taylor (PM): Quick clarification: will we call out competitor tradeoffs explicitly or keep it neutral and highlight our wins?
Alex (CEO): Be factual and direct. Don't call names, but call out scenarios where we materially outperform (e.g., multitenant latency SLOs, predictable cost under burst). Use numbers.
Ravi (Sales): I'll prep some competitive battlecards once we have the benchmarks + case studies.
Marta (People Ops): I'll create a short onboarding doc that links the one‑pager and recording for new hires.
Sam (Product): Anything else? I can draft the internal FAQ and a short copy pack for marketing.
Alex (CEO): Perfect — thanks all. If people have small questions, reply here. I'll follow up on any unresolved asks on Monday. :thumbsup:
Jordan (Eng): One tiny note — can we include sample config snippets in the public docs? e.g.:
```
model: redwood-open-7b
batching: latency-optimized
quant: q4_0
routing: region-prefer
```
That helps engineers onboard faster.
Priya (CTO): Love that. We'll add a "copy-paste" section for quickstarts.
Ravi (Sales): Also, can we get an enterprise one‑pager that explains Dedicated vs Private differences in plain language? Customers keep asking that.
Sam (Product): On it — I'll put a draft up in the product folder and ping SAs.
Alex (CEO): Thanks again. Closing loop: publish benchmarks + one‑pager + FAQ by next Friday (target). I'll drop a scheduled reminder.
Marta (People Ops): Noted — I'll include the link in the new hire checklist.
Priya (CTO): Thanks — closing the loop from eng side.
Alex (CEO): End of thread for now — appreciate the quick follow-ups.
